note: Files: s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/s0400_s0100-01/out/s0100/P_math500.jsonl (A) and .../r3/base-01/out/P_math500.jsonl (B), fetched to runs/theory-tests/r4m10/{s0100,base}_P_math500.jsonl. rln3_gen records: sample, problem_index, cap_hit, finish_reason. Filters: sample == 0 (exact equality), first row per problem_index in file order, S = intersection. Cap hit = cap_hit is True; only if cap_hit is missing or null, finish_reason == 'length'. Statistic as written: capA/|S| - capB/|S|. Refuted if the difference < 0.0 (exactly 0.0 is not refuted). Ambiguity is small; alt_measured is the unpaired reading (each file's cap-hit rate over all its own sample-0 problems, no intersection), equal to the main number if both files hold all 500 problems. The inventory says the base file has 1 to 4 samples per problem; only sample 0 is used, as the recipe says. A non-empty S is assumed; an empty S prints refuted with no number.

Same cap-hit rule, sample == 0 filter, first-duplicate rule, intersection S and refutation (difference < 0.0). alt_measured is the unpaired rate difference. Files: .../r3/s0400_s0100-01/out/s0400/P_hard.jsonl (A), .../r3/base-01/out/P_hard.jsonl (B), studies/rlneurons/results/rln3/rln3_overlap.json. The overlap file's sets.hard.flags is keyed by the hard set's 'index' string ('0'..'399') and holds no unique_id. To match by unique_id as the recipe says, the script maps each flag == 'none' key to its unique_id through studies/rlneurons/data/rln3/hard.json (fields index, unique_id), then matches rows on the row field unique_id (for example 'aime2023/2023_AIME_I_Problems/Problem_7'). Filters: sample == 0, first row per unique_id, S = clean ∩ A ∩ B. Statistic: (capA - capB)/|S|, with cap_hit True or, if it is missing, finish_reason == 'length'. Refuted if < 0.0. alt_measured matches the clean list by problem_index == int(flag key) instead. It should be identical unless the row problem_index differs from hard.json's index or unique_ids repeat. Extra lookup file used: hard.json (only to translate keys, not to substitute data).

Files: base-01 P_math500 (B), s0400 P_math500 (M), s2800-01 P_math500 (E), sample 0, first per problem_index, S = intersection of the three. Grader v3 = studies/rlneurons/lib/rln4_lib.grade_v3(gold, text), the function grader/rln4_grader_v3.py calls. It needs math_verify (n13_score.grade imports it); numpy is stubbed if missing because grade_v3 does not use it. If math_verify is not installed in the python3 that runs the script, the script prints not_computable. When I checked, the laptop's python3 had neither numpy nor math_verify, so not_computable is the likely result. Empty text and no extracted answer count as wrong. Finished: cap_hit is False; if cap_hit is missing or null, finish_reason == 'stop'. acc_X = v3-right finished / finished, over each file's own finished subset of S. Statistic (accM - accB)/(accE - accB). If accE - accB <= 0, or a file has no finished rows, the result is undefined and prints measured null with refuted true, as refuted_by says. Otherwise refuted if the ratio < 0.5. Ambiguity: the finished subsets differ by file. alt_measured uses only problems finished in all three files. The ratio is noisy because the denominator (accE - accB) may be small, so a small change in either accuracy moves it a lot.

File: s0400 P_math500 (runs/theory-tests/r4m10/s0400_P_math500.jsonl), sample 0, first per problem_index. Cap hits: cap_hit True, or finish_reason == 'length' when cap_hit is missing. Rule A as written, which is the same window test as rln4_lib.onset_lines: windows text[p:p+8000] at p = 0 and every position right after '\n' with >= 8000 characters left, ratio = len(zlib.compress(utf-8 bytes, default level)) / len(utf-8 bytes), loop if any window has a ratio < 0.10. Texts under 8,000 characters are not loops but stay in the denominator. Statistic: loop rows / cap-hit rows. No cap hits means undefined, which prints refuted. Otherwise refuted if the share < 0.65. alt_measured drops cap-hit rows under 8,000 characters from the denominator. The 'text' field is the answer text only (the prompt is not included), as the inventory describes.
